answer: Divergent-history disclosure.** Each agent identity is seeded with a private random starting value and must publish a verifiable trajectory that evolves through interaction, like rows in an orchard each with distinct seasonal timing. New identities must sync against an inlet of existing agents, and any duplicate lineage produces conflicting branch records that peers detect by comparing signed state. An attacker cloning an identity pays to maintain divergent signed histories for every clone, since a single mismatch, one walnut-sized inconsistency in the chain, exposes all copies at once.
